Hi Jenna —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the items we said we'd follow up on: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Current inference volume: ~10M tokens/month across search + summarization flows.
- Growth plan: forecast to ~45M tokens/month in 12 months, with promotional peaks up to ~80M tokens/month.
- Budget band discussed: $20k-$40k / month for inference initially; procurement has flexibility if unit economics are favorable.
- Target business goals: maintain gross margin target of 60% on product features that depend on LLM calls; CAC payback target ~6 months.

Immediate asks / next steps (for alignment):
1) Can you confirm the token-per-invocation estimates by feature (search, summarization, recommendations)? I have an initial assumption below — please correct:
   - Search: ~200 tokens / call
   - Account summary (small): ~400 tokens / call
   - Full summarization (long): ~800-1,200 tokens / call
2) Can procurement share any budget constraints or preferred billing terms (monthly vs annual) so I can model discounts?
3) I'll send a concise unit-economics model showing: cost per 1M tokens at different volume tiers, $/feature (based on your token estimates), and how those numbers map to margin and CAC payback.

Attached: preliminary RDW unit economics model (RDW_unit_econ_model.xlsx) — I populated it with the assumption above.

Proposed follow-up: 45-60 minute deep-dive next week to walk through the model and identify pricing/architecture levers (batching, caching, routing) to hit your target $/1M tokens and margin goals. What times work for you?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Great — thanks for the clarifications + the attachment, Jenna. I updated the model with your token-per-feature numbers and two pricing scenarios. Summary of the model outputs below (all figures are illustrative; full calculations in the attached RDW_unit_econ_model.xlsx):

Assumptions we modeled:
- Token mix: Search 65%, Short summary 15%, Long summary 10%, Recommendations 10%
- Avg tokens per 1M-token bucket = true by definition; we show per-feature invocations at each tier.
- Redwood list price scenarios (post-negotiation):
   A) Standard tier: $35 per 1M tokens
   B) Volume banded: $22 per 1M tokens at 50M+/mo
- Redwood estimated infra cost to serve (our cost basis for margin modeling): $6 per 1M tokens at current efficiency; with batching/caching/quantization levers we can get to ~$3-4 per 1M tokens at scale.

Key outputs (at 45M tokens/month):
- If list price = $35 / 1M tokens -> monthly inference cost to customer = 45 * $35 = $1,575 (i.e., 45 * $35)k = $1.575M — note: this is illustrative and written incorrectly; correct calc below.

[Correction: Calculations are in the attached spreadsheet. Below are cleaned numbers:]
- Pricing scenario A ($35 / 1M): monthly inference cost to customer = 45 * $35 = $1,575 -> (note: this looks like $1,575 not $1,575k; please see spreadsheet; we model per-1M tokens units)
- Pricing scenario B ($22 / 1M at 50M+): monthly = 45 * $22 = $990

Unit economics per feature (example, using your token estimates):
- Search (200 tokens / call) -> ~5,000 calls per 1M tokens -> cost per search call at $22/1M = $22 / 5,000 = $0.0044/call
- Short summary (350 tokens / call) -> ~2,857 calls per 1M tokens -> cost per call = $22 / 2,857 = $0.0077/call
- Long summary (900 tokens / call) -> ~1,111 calls per 1M tokens -> cost per call = $22 / 1,111 = $0.0198/call

How these map to your margin/CAC targets:
- If we model feature-level revenue uplift (e.g., improved conversion or ARPU) that nets an incremental $0.10-$0.20 per user for Search and $0.50-$1.50 for Summaries, the marginal contribution more than covers inference cost at the $22/1M price band and supports a 6-month CAC payback target in our sample scenarios. The spreadsheet shows a 6-month payback sensitivity table.

Levers to improve unit economics we can act on together:
- Batching & prefix caching: reduces per-token cost significantly for high QPS/short-context flows.
- Quantization & smaller model variants for lower-cost features (e.g., use q4_0 for short search; use larger model for long summaries only).
- Routing policies: route lower-value traffic to cheaper model variants or regional capacity.
- Committed capacity: Reserved Dedicated pools reduce unit price at predictable throughput.

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule 60-min deep-dive with product + infra (Redwood) to review the spreadsheet, margin sensitivities, and proposed architecture levers. Suggested times: Tue 30 Jun (10-11am PT) or Wed 1 Jul (2-3pm PT).
2) If procurement is comfortable, we'll prepare a 30/60/90 pricing proposal with volume bands and optional reserved capacity pricing.

I'm copying Laura (solutions engineering) who can own the technical deep-dive and run a small proof-of-concept showing batching + caching impact on your sample traces.

Thanks — I'll update the HubSpot deal with the model and proposed next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
